[P1] 西游记之八
高老庄

[P2] 高老庄
《西游记》之八
原著 吴承恩
改编 卢光照
绘画 陈缘督 朱丹枫
轩觀
印潮
河北美术出版社
内容提要
唐僧和他徒弟悟空到西天取经，走了六七天的荒山野路，这天来到高老庄投宿。
高老庄高太公的三女儿被一个妖怪强占了。高太公很是烦闷，到处请法师来捉妖，但都无效。正巧唐僧和他的徒弟悟空赶到这里，悟空想了个巧妙的办法，变成高太公的女儿，战胜了妖怪。
原来妖怪不是别人，正是后来帮助唐僧取经的猪八戒。

[P3] 1 唐僧、悟空师徒二人，辞别了观音院，继续向西天走去。走了六七天荒路，忽然看见一个人家。唐僧道：‘悟空，你看前边有座山庄，我们去借宿一宵怎样？’悟空道：‘待我先看看吉凶再说。’
2 悟空仔细看了一阵，说：‘师父请行，那是一村好人家，借宿无妨。’他们便向山庄走去，没有多时便到了村口。

[P4] 3 这时，正有一人急匆匆走出来。悟空一把扯住他道：
“哪里去？我问你这是什么地方？”那人哀求说：“我有要事，
不要拦我去路！”悟空道：“你若给我方便，有什么难事我也
可帮忙！
4 那人见挣不脱，便说道：“这庄叫高老庄。我是高太
公的家人，名叫高才。只因三年前我家小姐被一妖精霸占，
太公觉得招个妖精女婿不光彩，便要退亲。那妖精不但不
允，反把小姐关在后宅，不得和家人见面……”

[P5] 5 高才又说：‘高太公无奈，就命我四处请法师降妖。可是请了几个，都不管用！今天太公又差我出去访问仙道，若误了事定要重重责打。快放我去吧！’悟空听了，笑道：‘你太有造化了，不用远去，我保能降住那妖精！’
6 高才有些不信，悟空道：‘我们是东土大唐驾下差来的御弟圣僧，前往西天拜佛求经。一路上降了不止一个妖怪，你家这妖还能降不了？’高才这才有了几分相信，就在前边带路，引着他们到高太公家来。

[P6] 7 到了门前，高才道：‘二位长老请稍候一时，待我进去报告主人知道。’悟空便放下担子牵了马，师徒二人站立门旁等候。
8 高才进了大门，正好高太公出来，见面就喊：‘你这东西，叫你访问仙道，怎么又回来了！’高才把刚才的事一说，太公道：‘他们是哪里来的？’高才道：‘他们是东土大唐驾下差来的御弟圣僧，前往西天取经的。’

[P7] 9 太公一听是远路的和尚，心想，可能真有些手段。就急忙换了衣服，与高才出来迎接。远远地笑着作揖道：
“二位长老，这厢有礼了。”
10 太公见悟空相貌丑陋，就埋怨高才又招引来一个妖怪。悟空道：“你不要以貌取人，我老孙虽丑，但能降妖伏怪。”太公无奈，只好战兢兢地强打精神，把他们师徒引进家去。

[P8] 11 他们进了高宅，悟空把马拴在厅柱上，扯过一张椅子，叫师父坐下。然后又扯过一张椅子，坐在旁边。高太公道：“这个小长老，倒不认生。”悟空听了笑笑道：“若留我在你这住半年，还更不认生哩！
12 坐定以后，悟空问太公：“你家有几个妖怪？”太公道：“只有一个就够了！”悟空请他说说情况，也好捉拿。太公道：“我因无儿，三年前招了个养老女婿，初来时是个黑胖汉，后来就变成长嘴大耳的呆子……”

[P9] 13 “他不但能吃，还会呼风唤雨，云来雾去，吓得四邻不得安生。去年又把我女关在后院，半年不得见面，死活都难知道。因此知他是个妖精，要请个法师把他除掉。” 悟空道：“这个容易，夜晚替你拿住，让他退了婚就是。”
14 太公听了，问他要多少兵器，多少人？悟空道：“只要请几个老汉陪伴我师父，我好去降妖。兵器我随身带着。” 说着，从耳内取出一根绣花针，晃了一晃，变作一根碗口粗的金箍棒。

[P10] 15 这时天已黑了，悟空叫太公引路到后院去。到了那里，见一把大锁把门锁得牢牢的，太公正没奈何，悟空用金箍棒一捣，门就开了，里面黑洞洞的什么也看不见。
16 悟空道：“老高，你去叫你女儿一声，看在里面没有？”太公壮着胆子叫了几声，那女儿听是爹爹的声音，就有气无力地应了一声道：“爹爹，我在这里呢。”

[P11] 17 父女见面抱头痛哭。悟空道：‘不要哭，我问你，妖怪哪里去了？’女子道：‘不知道。这些天他天明出去，半夜回来。因为他知道父亲要赶退他，也十分小心。’悟空道：‘好吧，你们去前宅谈话，我在这里等他。’
18 等他们父女二人走后，悟空就摇身一变，变作那女子模样，独自个坐在房中，等候那妖怪。

[P12] 19 不多一会，一阵风来，吹得飞砂走石。风过处，半空中来了一个妖精，长嘴大耳，穿一件青不青蓝不蓝直襟布衫，系一条花手巾。悟空暗笑道：‘原来是这个东西！’悟空也不迎他，躺在床上装病，嘴里不住哼哼。
20 那怪不识真假，上前搂住就要亲嘴。悟空用手轻轻一推，把他推了一跤。妖精起来，陪笑道：‘姐姐，为何不高兴，想是我来迟了？’悟空道：‘只因我身上有些不舒服，你还缠人，怪烦的。快脱衣睡吧！’

[P13] 21 那妖精从地上爬起来后，要拉悟空上床。悟空轻轻一闪，那怪摸不着悟空，问道：‘姐姐你往哪里去了？快脱衣睡吧！’悟空道：‘我这就来。’那妖精果然先脱衣去睡。
22 悟空故意叹了口气，那怪问道：‘你今日为何叹气？我自到了你家，扫地通沟，搬砖运瓦，耕田耙地，拔麦插秧，我都干，还有什么不顺心的事儿？’悟空道：‘自嫁了你，连个姓名全无，爹爹也时常骂我！’

[P14] 23 那怪一听，连连安慰道：‘来来来，你爹爹再骂时，就告诉他，我家住在福陵山云栈洞，官名叫做猪刚鬣。’悟空暗喜道：‘这家伙真也老实，不动刑就都供了。这还愁拿不住他？’就上床来了。
24 悟空上了床，又道：‘听说我爹爹还要请法师拿你哩。’那怪笑道：‘别理他，我会变化，还有九齿铁钯，怕什么法师？’悟空道：‘他说要请五百年前大闹天宫的齐天大圣来拿你。’那怪吃惊道：‘那家伙有点法术，还是先躲躲吧！’

[P15] 25 说着，起身穿衣，开了门就要走。悟空一把扯住，抹了抹脸，现了原相。喝道：‘好妖怪，哪里走！你看我是谁？’那怪回头一看，见是悟空，早着了慌，刺啦一声，挣破了衣服，化阵狂风而去。
26 悟空举起金箍棒，望风打去。那怪化做万道金光，向云栈洞逃跑。悟空驾了云头，随后追来，叫道：‘哪里走！你若上天，我就赶到斗牛宫！你若入地，我就赶至枉死城，非把你捉住不可！’

[P16] 27 正在追赶，忽见前面一座高山，那怪钻入洞内，取出一把九齿钯来迎战。悟空怎能容情，两个在半山腰中打起来。
28 直到东方发白，那怪抵挡不住，化阵清风，又钻入洞中，把门紧闭，再不出来。悟空怕师父久等，决定先回去看看，再来捉拿妖怪。于是便驾起云头，奔往高老庄。

[P17] 29 悟空回到高老庄，见高太公和师父正在焦急，就把昨夜情形说了一遍，然后对太公说：‘你也太固执，他食量虽大，也替你干了活。他又不曾害你女儿，非赶他为何？’太公说：‘虽然没害，招个妖女婿也太难听……。’
30 高太公连连叩头，求他除掉妖精，唐僧也劝说，悟空笑道：‘师父，我是开开玩笑。这回我一定拿他回来。’说罢，一个跟头，早又到那山中。

[P18] 31 悟空来到云栈洞口，一顿金箍棒，把洞门打得稀烂。那怪正在洞内喘气，忽见悟空打进洞来，便拿起铁钯，迎了出来。
32 那怪厉声骂道：“这事与你何干，来管闲事？尝尝我这铁钯的厉害！”悟空道：“你这强占民女的罪犯，我还怕你？老孙不把头伸出来让你来打，不算好汉！”说完就伸过头来。

[P19] 33 那怪举起铁钯，朝悟空头上打来。只见金光四射，一点也不曾伤着头皮。那怪连打几下，看不见有半点损伤，吓得手软了。连说：‘好头！好头！’
34 悟空就把怎样大闹天宫，怎样被放在八卦炉中炼成了铜头铁臂的事说了一遍。那怪道：‘记得闹天宫时，你住在花果山水帘洞，怎么来到这里？莫非是我丈人把你请来的？’

[P20] 35 悟空又把自己保护唐僧法师西天求经，路过高老庄的事说给他听。那怪一听这话，便丢了铁钯，施礼道：‘那取经人在哪里？烦你引见引见。’
36 悟空奇怪道：‘你要见他怎的？’那怪道：‘我本是观音菩萨劝善，受了他的戒行，持斋把素，叫我跟随那取经人往西天求经，将功折罪，还得正果。烦你快快引见引见！’说着，伸手就要拉悟空走。

[P21] 37 悟空一把甩开道：‘你这家伙，还想欺诈于我，莫非要甩脱身之计。果真有意保护唐僧，可朝天发誓。’那怪听了，扑通一声跪下，对天发誓道：‘阿弥陀佛，我若不是真心实意，叫我犯了天条，碎尸万段！’
38 悟空见他赌咒发誓，又说：‘你把铁钯给我拿着。’那怪就把钯交给了悟空。悟空又拔了根毫毛，吹了口仙气，叫声‘变！’立即变作一根绳子，把那怪绑了起来。

[P22] 39 然后揪着他的耳朵，喝道：‘快走！快走！’那怪道：‘轻着点儿，你的手重，揪得我耳根子疼。’悟空道：‘不成！顾你不得！常言道：‘善猪恶拿。’只等见了师父，果有真心，方才放你。’
40 两个驾起云雾，顷刻来到了高老庄。悟空揪着那怪的耳朵，向那堂上一指道：‘你看那厅堂上坐的，就是我家师父。’

[P23] 41 那太公和众亲友见把那怪逮住，个个拍手称快。那怪走上前，双膝跪下，对唐僧叩头叫道：“师父，弟子失迎。早知道师父住在我丈人家，我早就来拜接了，何必费许多周折？
42 唐僧不顾那怪叩头，问悟空道：“悟空，你怎么降得他来拜我？”悟空才放了手，拿钉钯柄儿打着，喝道：“呆子，你说嘛！”那怪就又把菩萨劝善的事情，详细说了一遍。

[P24] 43 唐僧听了十分欢喜，叫悟空松了他的绑绳。悟空把身一抖，收回毫毛，绳子自然解开了。那怪重新礼拜唐僧，愿意跟随西去。
44 那怪又拜悟空为师兄。唐僧道：“既然做我徒弟，我与你起个法名，早晚好呼唤。”那怪道：“师父，菩萨早已与我起过法名，叫做猪悟能。”唐僧笑道：“好！好！你师兄叫悟空，你叫悟能，其实是我法门中的宗派。”

[P25] 45 那怪自是喜欢，又叩了个头道：“师父，我受了菩萨戒行，断了五荤三厌，在我丈人家持斋把素。如今见了师父，我开了斋吧。”唐僧道：“不行！不行！你既不吃五荤三厌，我再给你起个别名，叫做八戒。”
46 太公见那怪果真改邪归正，更是十分喜欢。便叫家僮安排酒宴，酬谢唐僧。八戒上前扯住太公道：“岳父，请我拙荆（称呼自己的妻子）出来拜见各位怎样？”

[P26] 47 悟空上前说道：‘师弟，你既做了和尚，以后别再提起那个“拙荆”吧。世间只有火居道士，那有火居和尚？我们且来坐下吃顿斋饭，快些赶路。’这时筵已摆好，太公请唐僧上坐，悟空、八戒坐于左右两旁；诸亲友也来陪客。
48 高太公把素酒满斟一杯，敬过天地，又来敬唐僧。唐僧因自幼不喝酒，谢绝了。悟空、八戒，虽然戒了五荤，但未戒酒，所以他两个便接过酒杯，和众人一起饮酒。

[P27] 49 师徒们吃过斋饭，高太公用一红漆盘子，托了二百两散碎金银，赠给三位长老为途中盘费；又托出三件褊衫，奉送穿用。唐僧道：‘我们是行脚僧，遇庄化缘，逢处求斋，怎敢受金银财帛？’
50 这时悟空走来，伸手抓了一把银子，叫道：‘高才，昨日累你引我师父，今日招了一个徒弟，无甚谢你，把这些碎金银送你，作为酬谢，拿去买草鞋穿。以后但有妖精再介绍几个，还要多谢你哩。’高才接了，叩头拜谢。

[P28] 51 高太公道：‘师父既不要金银，望将这粗衣收下，略表寸心。’唐僧又极力推辞。八戒道：‘师父，师兄，你们不要便罢，我的上衣，昨晚被师兄扯破了，希望我丈人能给我一件青布袈裟；鞋子也破了，与我一双新鞋子。’太公都照给了。
52 八戒喜得对太公施个礼道：‘我今天做和尚去了，不及一一面辞，还望原谅！丈人啊，还望你好生看待我的妻子，只怕我取不成经时，好来还俗，照旧与你做女婿过活。’

[P29] 53 悟空听了，喝道：‘笨货，却还胡说！’八戒笑道：‘不是胡说，只恐一时有些差错，落一个和尚误了做，老婆误了娶，两下都耽搁了？’
54 唐僧道：‘闲话少说，我们赶早上路是正经。’便收拾好行李，由八戒担着；备了白马，唐僧骑着；悟空肩扛金箍棒，前面引路。师徒三人，辞别了高太公和众人，向西天而去。欲知后事如何，请看第九册《黄风岭》。

[P1] Journey to the West, Volume Eight
Gao Lao Zhuang

[P2] Gao Laozhuang
The Eighth Volume of "Journey to the West"
Original Author: Wu Cheng'en
Adapted by: Lu Guangzhao
Illustrated by: Chen Yuandu, Zhu Danfeng
Xuan Guan
Yin Chao
Hebei Fine Arts Publishing House
Synopsis
Tang Sanzang and his disciple Wukong were traveling to the West to obtain scriptures. After walking six or seven days through desolate mountains and wild paths, they arrived at Gao Laozhuang to stay for the night.
The third daughter of Gao Taigong from Gao Laozhuang had been taken over by a demon. Gao Taigong was very distressed and had asked many monks to capture the demon, but all attempts failed. Just then, Tang Sanzang and his disciple Wukong arrived. Wukong devised a clever plan, transformed into Gao Taigong's daughter, and defeated the demon.
It turned out the demon was none other than Zhu Bajie, who would later help Tang Sanzang obtain the scriptures.

[P3] 1 Tang Sanzang and Wukong, master and disciple, bid farewell to the Guanyin Temple and continued westward. After walking six or seven days through desolate roads, they suddenly saw a household. Tang Sanzang said: 'Wukong, look, there's a village ahead. How about staying for the night?' Wukong replied: 'Let me first check for good or bad omens.'
2 Wukong carefully observed for a while and said: 'Master, please proceed. It's a good village, and it's safe to stay overnight.' They then walked toward the village and soon arrived at the village entrance.

[P4] 3 At this moment, a man hurried out. Wukong grabbed him and asked: 
"Where are you going? Tell me, what place is this?" The man pleaded: "I have urgent business, 
don't block my way!" Wukong replied: "If you let me help, I can assist you with any difficulty!"
4 Seeing he couldn't escape, the man said: "This is Gao Lao Zhuang. I am a servant of Master Gao, named Gao Cai. Three years ago, our young mistress was taken over by a demon. Master Gao felt it was shameful to marry a demon as a son-in-law, so he wanted to break off the engagement. The demon not only refused, but locked the young mistress in the back courtyard, preventing her from meeting her family..."

[P5] 5 Gao Cai said again: 'Master Gao had no choice but to send me out to find a master to subdue the demon. But I've already asked several, and none worked! Today, Master Gao sent me out again to seek out sages and immortals. If I fail, he will surely punish me severely. Please let me go!' Wukong, upon hearing this, laughed: 'You're very fortunate. You don't need to go far. I guarantee I can subdue that demon!'
6 Gao Cai was still somewhat doubtful. Wukong said: 'We are the holy monk sent by the Emperor of the Eastern Tang Dynasty, traveling to the Western Heaven to worship Buddha and seek scriptures. We have subdued more than one demon along the way. How could your demon be too difficult for us?' Only then did Gao Cai begin to believe a little, and he led the way ahead, guiding them to Master Gao's house.

[P6] 7 Upon reaching the gate, Gao Cai said, 'Please wait a moment, venerable masters, while I go in to inform the master.' Wukong then put down his burden and led the horse, while the master and disciple stood by the gate waiting.
8 Gao Cai entered the gate, and just then Master Gao came out, shouting, 'You rascal, I sent you to seek out the immortals, how come you're back already!' Gao Cai told him what had just happened. Master Gao asked, 'Where are they from?' Gao Cai replied, 'They are the imperial brother monks sent by the Tang Emperor from the Eastern Land, traveling to the Western Heaven to fetch scriptures.'

[P7] 9 The old master, upon hearing that they were monks traveling from afar, thought to himself, 'They might truly have some skills.' He hurriedly changed his clothes and came out to greet them with Gao Cai. From a distance, he smiled and bowed, saying: 
"Respected elders, I greet you with respect."
10 The old master, seeing Wukong's ugly appearance, blamed Gao Cai for bringing in another monster. Wukong said, "Don't judge a person by their appearance. Though I, Old Sun, am ugly, I can subdue demons and monsters." The old master, helpless, could only nervously muster his courage and lead the master and his disciples into his home.

[P8] 11 They entered the Gao household. Wukong tied the horse to a pillar in the hall, pulled over a chair, and told his master to sit down. Then he pulled over another chair and sat beside him. Old Master Gao said, "This young monk is not shy at all." Wukong laughed and replied, "If you let me stay here for half a year, I'd become even more unreserved!"
12 After settling down, Wukong asked the old man, "How many demons are there in your house?" The old man replied, "One is more than enough!" Wukong asked him to explain the situation so they could capture the demon. The old man said, "Since I have no son, three years ago I took in an old son-in-law. At first, he was a dark, fat man, but later he turned into a foolish fellow with a long mouth and big ears..."

[P9] 13 "He not only eats a lot, but also summons wind and rain, brings clouds and fog, scaring the neighbors to death. Last year, he locked my daughter in the back courtyard for half a year, and I didn't know if she was alive or dead. Therefore, I know he is a demon, and I want to hire a sorcerer to get rid of him." Wukong said, "That's easy. I'll catch him at night and make him break off the marriage." 
14 The old man listened and asked, "How many weapons and how many people do you need?" Wukong said, "Just ask a few old men to accompany my master, and I'll go to subdue the demon. I carry my weapons with me." Saying that, he took out a needle from his ear, waved it, and turned it into a golden cudgel as thick as a bowl.

[P10] 15 It was already dark. Wukong asked Old Gao to lead the way to the back courtyard. When they arrived, they saw a large lock securing the door tightly. Old Gao was at a loss, but Wukong used his Golden Cudgel to pry it open. Inside, it was pitch black and nothing could be seen.
16 Wukong said, "Old Gao, go call your daughter and see if she's inside." Old Gao, summoning his courage, called out a few times. The daughter, hearing her father's voice, weakly responded, "Dad, I'm here."

[P11] 17 The father and daughter met and wept bitterly. Wukong said, 'Don't cry. Tell me, where is the demon?' The girl replied, 'I don't know. These days he goes out at dawn and returns at midnight. Because he knows Father wants to drive him away, he is also very careful.' Wukong said, 'Alright, you two go talk at the front house. I'll wait for him here.'
18 After the father and daughter left, Wukong transformed himself, turning into the girl's appearance, and sat alone in the room, waiting for the demon.

[P12] 19 Not long after, a gust of wind came, blowing sand and stones. In the wind, a demon appeared from the air, with a long snout and big ears, wearing a blueish-green straight-collared shirt and a floral handkerchief. Wukong secretly laughed: 'So this is the creature!' Wukong didn't greet him, lying in bed pretending to be sick, groaning continuously.
20 The demon, not recognizing the fake, rushed forward to embrace and kiss. Wukong gently pushed him, sending him tumbling. The demon got up and smiled: 'Sister, why are you unhappy? Perhaps I'm late?' Wukong replied: 'I'm just feeling a bit unwell. You're still bothering me, it's annoying. Go change and sleep!'

[P13] 21 The demon got up from the ground and tried to pull Wukong onto the bed. Wukong lightly dodged, and the demon, unable to touch him, asked, 'Sister, where did you go? Hurry up and take off your clothes and sleep!' Wukong replied, 'I'm coming right away.' The demon then indeed took off his clothes and went to sleep.
22 Wukong deliberately sighed. The demon asked, 'Why are you sighing today? Since I came to your home, I've swept the floor, cleared the ditches, carried bricks and tiles, plowed the fields, and harvested wheat and planted seedlings. I've done everything. What's still bothering you?' Wukong replied, 'Since I married you, I don't even have a name, and my father often scolds me!'

[P14] 23 The monster, upon hearing this, comforted him repeatedly: 'Come, come, come. When your father scolds you again, tell him I live in the Cloudy Stack Cave on Fuling Mountain, and my official name is Zhu Ganglie.' Wukong secretly rejoiced: 'This fellow is truly honest; he confessed everything without any torture. How could I possibly fail to capture him?' Then he climbed onto the bed.
24 Wukong got onto the bed and said: 'I heard my father is going to invite a master to catch you.' The monster laughed: 'Don't worry about him. I can transform, and I have the Nine-Toothed Rake. What do I fear from any master?' Wukong replied: 'He said he's going to invite the Great Sage Equal to Heaven, who caused chaos in Heaven five hundred years ago, to catch you.' The monster was startled and said: 'That fellow has some magic. I'd better hide for now!'

[P15] 25 Speaking, he got up, dressed himself, and was about to leave. Wukong grabbed him, wiped his face, and revealed his true form. He shouted, 'You monster, where do you think you're going! Do you know who I am?' The demon turned around, saw Wukong, panicked, tore his clothes with a 'ripping' sound, and fled in a gust of wind.
26 Wukong raised his golden cudgel and struck at the wind. The demon transformed into myriad beams of golden light and fled toward Cloud-Stack Cave. Wukong mounted the clouds and chased after, shouting, 'Where do you think you're going! If you go to heaven, I'll chase you to the Palace of the Ox and Bull! If you go underground, I'll pursue you to the City of the Dead, and I won't stop until I catch you!'

[P16] 27 While chasing, he suddenly saw a tall mountain ahead. The monster dived into a cave and pulled out a nine-toothed rake to fight. How could Wukong show mercy? The two fought fiercely in the middle of the mountain.
28 Until the east turned white, the monster could not withstand the attack, turned into a gust of wind, and dived back into the cave, tightly closing the door and not coming out. Wukong, fearing his master had been waiting too long, decided to return first to check, and then come back to capture the monster. So he mounted the clouds and rushed toward Gao's village.

[P17] 29 Wukong returned to Gao's village and saw Master Gao and his master in distress. He recounted the events of the previous night, then said to Master Gao: 'You're too stubborn. He may eat a lot, but he also does your work. He hasn't harmed your daughter, so why drive him away?' Master Gao replied: 'Even if he hasn't harmed her, marrying a demon groom is too shameful...'
30 Master Gao bowed repeatedly, begging him to eliminate the demon. Tang Sanzang also pleaded. Wukong laughed: 'Master, I was just joking. This time, I'll definitely bring him back.' Saying that, he flipped a somersault and was soon back in the mountains.

[P18] 31 Wukong arrived at the entrance of Yunzhan Cave and, with a flurry of his Golden Cudgel, smashed the cave door to pieces. The demon, who was panting inside, suddenly saw Wukong breaking in and immediately grabbed his iron rake, rushing out to meet him.
32 The demon shouted angrily, "What business is this of yours? Why meddle in my affairs? Taste the power of my iron rake!" Wukong replied, "You criminal who has taken a civilian woman by force—do I fear you? If I don't stick my head out for you to hit, I'm not a true man!" He then extended his head.

[P19] 33 The monster raised his iron rake and struck at Wukong's head. Golden light flashed, and not a single hair was harmed. The monster struck several times, seeing no damage at all, and his hands grew weak with fear. He kept saying, 'Good head! Good head!'
34 Wukong then told the monster how he had caused chaos in Heaven and how he had been placed in the Eight-Trigram Furnace, forged into a head of copper and arms of iron. The monster said, 'I remember when you caused chaos in Heaven, you lived in the Water Curtain Cave on Flower-Fruit Mountain. How did you come here? Could it be that my father-in-law invited you?'

[P20] 35 Wukong told the demon again about protecting Master Tang on his journey to the West to obtain scriptures, and how he had passed through Gao Lao Zhuang. Upon hearing this, the demon dropped his iron rake and bowed, saying, 'Where is that scripture-seeker? Please introduce me to him.'
36 Wukong asked curiously, 'Why do you want to see him?' The demon replied, 'I was persuaded by Bodhisattva Guanyin to do good, took her precepts, observed vegetarianism, and was told to follow that scripture-seeker to the West to obtain scriptures, to atone for my sins and attain enlightenment. Please quickly introduce me to him!' Saying this, he reached out to grab Wukong.

[P21] 37 Wukong pushed him away and said, 'You rascal, still trying to deceive me? Are you planning to escape? If you truly intend to protect Master Tang, swear to heaven.' The demon, upon hearing this, fell to his knees with a thud and swore to heaven, 'Amitabha, if I am not sincere, let me break the heavenly laws and be torn into a million pieces!'
38 Seeing the demon swear an oath, Wukong said, 'Give me your iron rake.' The demon handed the rake to Wukong. Wukong then plucked a hair, blew a breath of divine air, shouted 'Change!', and instantly it turned into a rope, which he used to bind the demon.

[P22] 39 Then, grabbing his ears, he shouted: 'Hurry! Hurry!' The demon said: 'Be gentle, your grip is too hard, it hurts my ears.' Wukong replied: 'No way! I can't spare you! As the saying goes, 'Good pigs are caught harshly.' I'll only let you go after seeing my master, and only if you truly mean it.
40 The two rode on clouds and arrived at Gao's Village in an instant. Wukong, still grabbing the demon's ears, pointed toward the hall and said: 'Look at the one sitting in that hall—that's my master.'

[P23] 41 The old master and his relatives saw the monster caught and clapped their hands in delight. The monster stepped forward, knelt down, and bowed to Tang Sanzang, saying, "Master, I apologize for not welcoming you properly. If I had known you were staying at my in-laws' house, I would have come to greet you long ago. Why go through so much trouble?"
42 Tang Sanzang ignored the monster's bow and asked Wukong, "Wukong, how did you manage to make him bow to me?" Wukong then let go, hit the monster with the handle of his rake, and shouted, "Fool, you tell him!" The monster then recounted the story of how the Bodhisattva had persuaded him to turn good, in detail.

[P24] 43 The monk was very pleased and told Wukong to loosen the bindings. Wukong shook his body, retracted his hairs, and the ropes naturally came undone. The demon bowed to the monk again and expressed his willingness to follow westward.
44 The demon then bowed to Wukong as his elder brother. The monk said, "Since you are my disciple, I will give you a Dharma name so I can call you easily." The demon replied, "Master, the Bodhisattva has already given me a Dharma name: Zhu Wuneng." The monk laughed, "Good! Good! Your elder brother is Wukong, and you are Wuneng—truly in line with our Dharma lineage."

[P25] 45 The monster was delighted and bowed again, saying, “Master, I have received the Bodhisattva’s precepts, given up the five pungent vegetables and three forbidden meats, and have been observing a vegetarian diet at my in-laws’ house. Now that I’ve seen you, Master, may I break my fast?” The monk replied, “No! No! Since you don’t eat the five pungent vegetables and three forbidden meats, I’ll give you another name—Bajie.”
46 The old man saw that the monster had truly reformed and was very pleased. He ordered his servant to prepare a banquet to thank the monk. Bajie stepped forward and grabbed the old man, saying, “Father-in-law, may I bring my wife (referring to his own wife) out to greet everyone?”

[P26] 47 Wukong stepped forward and said, 'Younger brother, now that you've become a monk, don't mention that "chuzheng" again. In the world, there are only fire-residing Taoists, but no fire-residing monks? Let's sit down and have a vegetarian meal, then hurry on our journey.' At this time, the banquet was already set. The old man invited Master Tang to sit in the center, with Wukong and Bajie seated on either side; relatives and friends also came to accompany the guests.
48 The old man of Gao filled a cup with vegetarian wine, offered it to heaven and earth, and then presented it to Master Tang. Master Tang, who had never drunk alcohol since childhood, declined. Wukong and Bajie, although they had abstained from the five pungent vegetables, had not abstained from alcohol, so the two of them accepted the cups and drank with everyone else.

[P27] 49 After the disciples had finished their vegetarian meal, Gao Taigong placed two hundred taels of scattered silver and gold on a red lacquered tray, offering it to the three elders as travel expenses; he also presented three plain robes for them to wear. Tang Sanzang said, 'We are wandering monks, begging for alms at villages and seeking meals wherever we go—how could we dare accept silver and gold?'
50 At this moment, Wukong came over, grabbed a handful of silver, and called out, 'Gao Cai, yesterday you helped me bring my master here, and today I've taken on a new disciple. I have nothing to thank you with, so take this scattered silver and gold as a reward, and use it to buy straw shoes. If you can introduce more demons in the future, I'll thank you even more!' Gao Cai accepted it and bowed gratefully.

[P28] 51 Gao Taigong said, 'Master, since you don't want gold or silver, please accept this coarse garment as a small token of my heart.' Tang Sanzang again tried to refuse. Zhu Bajie said, 'Master, elder brother, if you don't want it, that's fine. My upper garment was torn last night by my elder brother. I hope my father-in-law can give me a blue cloth robe; my shoes are also broken, so please give me a new pair.' Gao Taigong gave him everything.
52 Zhu Bajie happily bowed to Gao Taigong and said, 'Today I am going to become a monk. I cannot bid farewell to everyone one by one, so please forgive me! Father-in-law, I hope you will take good care of my wife. If I fail to obtain the scriptures, I will return to secular life and continue to be your son-in-law.'

[P29] 53 Wukong heard and shouted, 'Fool, are you still talking nonsense?' Bajie laughed, 'It's not nonsense. I'm just afraid that if something goes wrong, the monk might miss his chance to become a monk, and the wife might miss her chance to get married—both sides would be delayed.'
54 Tang Sanzang said, 'Enough chit-chat, we must set off early.' He packed the luggage, which Bajie carried; prepared the white horse, which Tang Sanzang rode; Wukong shouldered the golden cudgel and led the way. The three disciples bid farewell to Gao Taigong and the others, and set off toward the Western Heaven. To learn what happens next, please read Volume Nine, 'The Yellow Wind Ridge.'

full_summary_zh:
[P1] 本页为《西游记》连环画第八册的封面，标题为“高老庄”，画面描绘了孙悟空与猪八戒在高老庄的场景，唐僧、孙悟空、猪八戒、沙僧等角色在室内，孙悟空正与一人互动。
[P2] 本页为《西游记》连环画第八册《高老庄》的封面及内容提要，介绍了唐僧师徒来到高老庄，孙悟空化身为高太公女儿智斗并降服妖怪（即猪八戒）的故事梗概。
[P3] 唐僧与孙悟空师徒二人辞别观音院后，行至荒野，发现一座山庄。唐僧提议借宿，孙悟空先观察后认为安全，二人遂前往村口。
[P4] 孙悟空在高老庄拦住一名急匆匆的男子，询问此处地名，男子自称高才，向孙悟空诉说高家小姐被妖精霸占、不得与家人相见的遭遇。
[P5] 高才向孙悟空诉说高太公请法师降妖未果，请求放他离开；孙悟空自信能降服妖精，并自报身份为唐僧徒弟，高才半信半疑后带他们前往高太公家。
[P6] 高才带唐僧师徒来到高老庄门前，向主人报告后，师徒二人在门外等候。高才进入大门后，高太公出来责问，高才解释并说明唐僧师徒是奉旨西天取经的御弟圣僧。
[P7] 高太公听说唐僧师徒是远道而来的和尚，急忙换衣迎接，但见到孙悟空相貌丑陋后心生疑虑，埋怨高才又引来妖怪。孙悟空自辩能降妖伏怪，高太公无奈之下只得强打精神将他们师徒迎进家中。
[P8] 唐僧师徒进入高太公家中，孙悟空将马拴好并坐下，高太公对孙悟空不认生表示惊讶，孙悟空幽默回应。随后，孙悟空询问妖怪情况，高太公描述了妖怪从黑胖汉变为长嘴大耳呆子的过程。
[P9] 高太公向孙悟空详细描述妖怪的恶行，孙悟空表示可当晚捉拿并让其退婚；高太公询问所需人手和兵器，孙悟空表示只需几个老汉陪伴师父，自己随身携带兵器，并当场从耳中取出绣花针变作金箍棒。
[P10] 夜幕降临，孙悟空带高太公到后院，用金箍棒撬开被锁住的门，发现里面漆黑一片。随后，孙悟空让高太公叫女儿，女儿听到父亲声音后有气无力地回应，表明她被关在院内。
[P11] 父女相见后痛哭，孙悟空询问妖怪下落并安排高太公父女去前宅谈话，自己则变作女子模样在房中等候妖怪。
[P12] 孙悟空变作女子模样在房中等候，妖怪现身时，孙悟空假装生病，待妖怪上前亲近时将其推倒，并假意抱怨其烦扰，诱其脱衣，为捉拿妖怪做准备。
[P13] 孙悟空变作女子模样诱骗妖怪，妖怪上当后欲拉其上床，孙悟空假装答应并故意叹气，妖怪询问原因，孙悟空抱怨自己无名无姓且被父亲责骂，以激怒妖怪。
[P14] 孙悟空化身为女子诱骗妖怪，妖怪在得知其父要请法师捉拿自己后，因害怕齐天大圣而惊慌，打算躲藏。
[P15] 孙悟空识破妖怪真身，将其擒住后妖怪化风逃走，孙悟空随即驾云追赶，并发誓无论妖怪逃向天上还是地下，都要将其捉拿归案。
[P16] 孙悟空追赶妖怪至高山，妖怪钻入洞中取出九齿钯迎战，二人在半山腰激战。天亮后妖怪不敌，化风逃回洞中闭门不出，孙悟空担心师父久等，便先返回高老庄。
[P17] 孙悟空回到高老庄，向高太公和唐僧解释昨夜情况，高太公仍因妖怪身份而担忧，孙悟空承诺再次捉拿妖怪后便重返山中。
[P18] 孙悟空来到云栈洞口，用金箍棒砸烂洞门，妖怪持铁钯迎战，孙悟空挑衅对方，主动伸头迎击。
[P19] 孙悟空与妖怪交战，妖怪用铁钯攻击孙悟空头部，但因孙悟空头硬如铜铁，毫发无损，妖怪惊惧。随后孙悟空讲述自己大闹天宫及炼成铜头铁臂的经历，妖怪怀疑他是被自己岳父请来捉拿自己的。
[P20] 孙悟空向妖怪讲述自己保护唐僧西天取经的经历，妖怪听后放下武器，请求孙悟空引见唐僧，并声称自己受观音菩萨点化，愿改过自新，跟随取经人赎罪求正果。
[P21] 孙悟空要求妖怪发誓真心保护唐僧，妖怪发誓后，孙悟空取走其铁钯并用毫毛变出绳子将其绑缚。
[P22] 孙悟空揪着妖怪的耳朵，将其带往高老庄，并向妖怪指明唐僧在厅堂上坐着，准备让妖怪面见师父。
[P23] 妖怪被孙悟空带回高老庄，向唐僧叩头请罪，唐僧未理睬，孙悟空责问妖怪并逼其再次讲述被观音菩萨点化改过自新的经过。
[P24] 唐僧同意收服妖怪为徒，孙悟空松开绑绳，妖怪重新礼拜唐僧并表示愿随西行。随后妖怪拜孙悟空为师兄，唐僧为其取法名“猪悟能”，并称其与悟空同属法门宗派。
[P25] 猪八戒向唐僧请求开斋，唐僧为其取名“八戒”；高太公见其真心改过，设宴款待，并被八戒请求让妻子出来拜见众人。
[P26] 孙悟空劝猪八戒改掉俗念，众人在高太公家设宴款待唐僧师徒。唐僧因不饮酒而谢绝，孙悟空和猪八戒则与众人一同饮酒。
[P27] 师徒们在高太公家吃过斋饭后，高太公欲赠金银和衣物作为盘缠，唐僧婉拒。孙悟空则抓取部分银子赠予高太公作为酬谢，并戏言若再介绍妖精，会多谢他，高太公接银叩谢。
[P28] 高太公欲赠粗衣给唐僧以表心意，唐僧推辞，猪八戒则请求丈人给予新衣和新鞋，高太公一一应允。随后猪八戒向高太公辞行，请求善待其妻，并表示若取经不成将归来还俗续娶。
[P29] 孙悟空责备猪八戒胡说，猪八戒解释担心耽误修行与婚事；随后唐僧催促启程，师徒三人收拾行李，辞别高太公和众人，向西天出发。
